notes:
Structural assertions the canary evaluates against a live surface (DEL-92). These are NOT extraction rules: they answer 'does this page still look like the page the pack was written for'. A pack can resolve every field and still be reading the wrong element, and a rising fallback rate tells you a strategy moved but not what moved. These say what changed.

Evaluated against a serialised subtree, so the same file runs against the fixture corpus and against a live canary with no difference in code path.

assertions.notes: The review feed exists at all. If this fails nothing else is worth evaluating — the page is not a listing page, and every other assertion would report a confusing secondary failure.

At least one review node. Zero here with the surface present is the exact ambiguity §21.9 turns on: either the listing genuinely has no reviews, or the node selector broke. The canary runs against a listing known to have reviews, so zero means the selector broke.

The accessible rating label is still present. This is P1 of the cascade and the only locale-independent source of the numeric value; losing it drops every record onto the fallbacks, which is invisible in the payload and obvious here.

Contributor links still key on the /contrib/ path shape. A warning rather than an error because author_name has a labelled strategy above this one — but if this vanishes, author identity is running on its last strategy.
The relative date element. Required by §21.3, and a missing date quarantines the record — so this failing predicts a quarantine spike rather than explaining one after the fact.

A challenge form must NOT be present. Stated as a maximum because the dangerous direction here is presence, not absence — and a challenge reaching the assertion stage at all means detection did not fire first, which is CHAL-01's failure.
